subject.title: Feature Request: Scoped / Script-Limited Agent Mode (Cost-Controlled + Predictable Execution)

question: What native scoped-automation contract should OpenClaw expose for cron/script-limited agent runs, and which pieces should remain separate component issues?
rationale: The request defines execution authority, spend admission, persisted state, and public schema/CLI contracts, so automation should not choose the permanent product and security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design shared native scoped mode
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella tracker and require a maintainer-approved design that unifies script registry, dry-run preview, tool policy, context mode, budget admission, and run receipts across cron and hooks.

options.title: Split into component trackers
options.body: Narrow or close this only after maintainers explicitly choose narrower issues as canonical owners for cost, dry-run, cron schema, and tool or elevated scoping.

options.title: Use plugin/API boundary only
options.body: Route optional workflow packaging to plugins or ClawHub only if maintainers confirm no missing core execution-policy or budget-admission API is needed.

recommendation.title: Design shared native scoped mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella tracker and require a maintainer-approved design that unifies script registry, dry-run preview, tool policy, context mode, budget admission, and run receipts across cron and hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: He already kept this issue open as the broad scoped automation tracker and is actively touching adjacent cron contract surfaces in an open PR.
